subject.title: [Feature] Allow per-binding tool restrictions (tools.deny) in route/ACP bindings

question: Should OpenClaw support route/ACP binding-scoped `tools.allow`/`tools.deny` as a core security/config boundary, and if so where should it sit relative to group, sender, session, gateway-scope, and conversation-identity policy?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but adding a new config-enforced tool boundary changes security semantics and overlaps multiple existing and planned policy surfaces.

options.title: Design binding-scoped policy
options.body: Accept the feature direction, specify precedence, and implement schema plus runtime enforcement together with route/ACP tests.

options.title: Use existing policy surfaces
options.body: Close or narrow this request by documenting that operators should use group, sender, session, or gateway-scope policy instead of binding policy.

options.title: Defer to conversation identity work
options.body: Keep the item blocked behind the broader capability-profile and identity-mode work so binding policy is decided as part of that design.

recommendation.title: Design binding-scoped policy
recommendation.body: Accept the feature direction, specify precedence, and implement schema plus runtime enforcement together with route/ACP tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent conversation capability and identity-mode work is the closest maintainer-visible policy surface for this decision.
